topic: Through-traffic infiltration of access roads (environmental cells)
idea: Planning networks as hierarchy (primary distributor, district distributor 50-60 km/h, local distributor, access road) so that each class intersects only with its own class or one above/below; roads bounding self-contained zones (cells) keep non-essential traffic out; grid layouts are less safe than networks that segregate access and movement; through trips should be routed on distributors and made inconvenient on access roads (cul-de-sacs, loops, meandering, residential roads over 100 m kinked); direct frontage access banned on district distributors and above; 3-leg rather than 4-leg junctions on access roads.
does: Defines cells from the road hierarchy (low-class roads enclosed by higher-class roads), then from a run or from route assignment counts the share of vehicles on local/access roads whose origin and destination are both outside the cell (rat-running), the share of vehicle-km on each class, and the speed of through traffic on access roads; flags cells where a shortcut exists that is faster than the distributor and suggests closures (delete road, one-way, speed cut) to test with run_experiment.
inputs: road class or speed/lane-derived class, run vehicle origin/destination and path, cell definition
outputs: through-traffic share per cell and road, shortcut roads ranked by diverted veh-km, suggested treatments
existing: partial: critical_links, network_indices (detour index), assign_routes (route choice); no hierarchy cell or infiltration metric
notes: Road class is a stored-only label in ACMS; infer from speed and lanes. Pairs with check_road_hierarchy (SRC_022-001) which checks class jumps at junctions.

topic: Free-flow speed reduction from lane width and surface condition
idea: Expected reduction in 85th percentile free speed from a flat, straight, smooth, wide road: by carriageway width (Table 4.02, ORN 6): 5.0 m or more 0 km/h, 4.5 m about 4, 4.0 m 7, 3.5 m 11, 3.0 m 15, 2.5 m 19; by surface: good paved 4?, potholed paved 6?, good gravel 8?, average gravel 15?, corrugated about 15 (values as printed are jumbled in the extraction, order good paved < pot-holed < gravel < corrugated); design class table (Table 4.01): class A arterial 5,000-15,000 ADT paved 6.5 m + 2.5 m shoulders, 120/100/85 km/h level/rolling/mountainous; class B 1,000-5,000: 100/85/70; C 400-1,000: 85/70/60; D 100-400: 70/60/50; E and F access roads 3.0 m and 2.5-3.0 m. Design speed should match estimated actual speed (consistency); relaxations need warnings and stepped design speeds.
does: Gives each road an expected free-flow speed from its width and condition (and curvature) instead of the posted limit alone: the simulation caps desired speed per road by this estimate and the assistant reports where posted speed exceeds estimated actual speed or where consecutive roads differ by more than one design class.
inputs: road lane width, surface condition, curvature, posted speed, design class
outputs: estimated 85th percentile free speed per road, reduction table row, mismatch flags
existing: partial: curve speed vs radius in analyse_network; vehicles use the road speed limit with Krauss/LC2013; no width or surface effect
notes: Exact table values need the PDF figures; the text extraction scrambles the surface-condition column. Useful for developing-country scenarios (potholed, gravel roads).

topic: Junction control type recommender with safety-driven rules
idea: Intersection selection (Table 4.11, Fig 4.69): grade separation for high flows (minimal delay, expensive); signals for low-medium flows, handle heavy turns with filters, need all drivers to know the signal; roundabout for low-medium flows, good for turners but poor for cyclists and slow vehicles, needs more space; priority give-way/stop for low flows, high delay to minor road, needs stopping sight distance on the major road. Rules: simplest proven design that local drivers understand; terminating-road (give way on the T stem) rule in rural areas; GIVE WAY not STOP where sight lines are good (STOP signs ignored breed disrespect); staggered crossroads have better safety records than straight crossroads, right-left stagger for driving on the left; sideswipes at straight crossroads at night when the view across hides the priority junction; capacity must not be gained at the expense of safety; multi-lane approaches on priority junctions are hazardous.
does: For each junction compares the demand (major and minor flows per hour from the OD routing), speeds, lane counts, pedestrian and cyclist presence and sight distance, and recommends priority, roundabout, signal or grade separation by the table rules; reports the saturation or delay estimate for each option and the safety notes (stagger, multilane approach, STOP vs give way); with the assistant's set_junction_control it can apply and test the change by paired runs.
inputs: junction approach flows, speeds, lanes, legs, bus/pedestrian demand, existing control
outputs: recommended control per junction with reasons, ranked alternatives, estimated delay/v/c per option
existing: partial: set_junction_control (signalised / roundabout / uncontrolled), optimise_signals, junction capacity measured in simulation; no recommendation rule
notes: The flow thresholds of Fig 4.69 are in a graph not extracted; use HCM capacity numbers (roundabout entry thresholds from Green Book SRC_022 s9.10) as the thresholds.

topic: Blackspot ranking with equivalent accident numbers and rates
idea: Identify hazardous sites objectively: intersections ranked by average annual accidents (3-year mean minimum because site counts are rare random events that vary widely year to year), links by accidents per km per year (accident density); crashes within 30 m of an intersection count as intersection crashes; severity weighting with Equivalent Accident Numbers EAN = 12 fatal, 3 injury, 1 damage-only (South Korea, Trinidad and Tobago), or by cost; rates per million vehicles entering an intersection or per million vehicle-km when flows exist; prefer sites with repeated similar crash types (3 injury + 3 damage with a common cause) over a single random fatal; blackspot flowchart with continuous monitoring and before/after evaluation (Fig 6.03).
does: Turns analyse_safety output over several seeds into a blackspot list: conflicts assigned to the nearest junction if within 30 m else to the link; severity-weighted score (severe conflict = 12 equivalent, ordinary = 1, with the weights editable); per million entering vehicles for junctions and per km for links; mean and spread over at least three seeds as the 'three-year average'; flags sites dominated by one severe event as unreliable and sites with repeated same-type conflicts as treatable; the same list before and after an edit gives a before/after safety evaluation.
inputs: run ids (several seeds) of the same network, severity weights, 30 m threshold
outputs: ranked sites with weighted score, rate, type mix, consistency across seeds, treatability flag, before/after change
existing: partial: analyse_safety (rear-end conflicts per road, per million vehicle-km, severe conflicts, performance index)
notes: Simulated conflicts are rear-end TTC only; crossing conflicts and post-encroachment time are not built (not_built), so junction ranking under-reads turning conflicts.

topic: Vehicle-class restrictions and lorry management scenarios
idea: Traffic management options on existing roads: parking and loading bans at peak, closures and turn bans to keep through traffic out of areas, one-way systems (care: higher speeds), HGV control by advisory routing, width barriers narrowing to 2.2 m (excludes lorries), height gauges, time-of-day delivery windows, area-wide lorry bans or cordons, hazardous-goods routing on main roads only, bus lanes and bus gates; limited set of standard speed limits (50, 80, 100, 120 km/h) and area 30 km/h zones; speed limits work only with enforcement or physical measures.
does: Assistant tool to allow or disallow vehicle types on a road (and by time window), e.g. ban trucks from a residential cell, give buses an exclusive lane, or set a school-zone 30 km/h; routes re-assign (assign_routes) respecting the restriction and run_experiment reports the effect on trip time, through traffic in the cell and safety.
inputs: road ids, vehicle types allowed or banned, optional time window, speed limit change
outputs: edit set, rerouted flows, comparison KPIs
existing: partial: update_roads (speed, lanes, one-way/reversed), delete_objects; no per-class access or time-window restriction
notes: SUMO supports allow/disallow vehicle classes per lane; ACMS has vehicle types (bus, truck, trailer, motorcycle, bike).

topic: Before/after evaluation with side-effect and migration scan
idea: Evaluate countermeasures by behaviour, not crashes only: measure what the device is meant to change (speed, turn compliance, crossing use) before and after; watch for new crash types offsetting the saving, for underlying traffic growth, regression to the mean (blackspots improve without treatment), control sites, and accident migration to alternative routes; remedial schemes often cut targeted crashes 40-50%, sometimes 80%; temporary cheap trials (painted islands, drums) allow fine-tuning before permanent works.
does: Wraps run_experiment for a design change with a standard report: the intended-effect KPI (e.g. speed at the site, conflicts of the targeted type), the same KPIs on neighbouring and parallel roads within a radius (diversion, queue migration), network totals, and an explicit list of KPIs that got worse; with paired seeds it states that regression to the mean is controlled because the baseline is rerun on identical seeds, and for observed data in calibrate_demand it warns when only a single year of counts is given.
inputs: baseline and variant scenarios, seeds, intended-effect KPI, radius for neighbours
outputs: intended effect with CI, side-effect table (neighbouring roads, other conflict types), worsened-KPI list, verdict
existing: partial: run_experiment (paired t-tests, scenarios), compare_runs (headline figures); no neighbourhood side-effect scan
notes: The per-road results in read_results already have the data; the tool is a report layer.

idea: Accident analysis by dominant pattern: accident grid or collision diagram (manoeuvres by type, time of day, vehicle type, weather) to find the few predominant types, then problem-oriented remedies: remove the conflict, improve visibility, or reduce speed; remedy tables for skidding, roadside obstacles, pedestrian conflicts, darkness, poor visibility (Table 6.01), rural (turn prohibition, channelisation, acceleration/deceleration lanes, protected turns, overtaking zones, intersection conspicuity, speed devices) and urban (channelisation, signals, roundabouts when turns are 20% or more and flows balanced, parking control, crossings) situations (Table 6.02, 6.03); crossing and merging streams are more crash-prone than parallel or diverging ones.
does: Breaks the simulated conflicts of a site into movement classes (rear-end in queue, rear-end at a turn, hard braking at a signal change, merge), by time of day and vehicle type, picks the dominant class, and returns the matching remedy from a small table (e.g. rear-end at turn: add a turn pocket or signal phase; speed at curve: speed limit or radius; merge: lengthen taper) as candidate edits the assistant can test; the LLM explains the diagnosis.
inputs: analyse_safety conflict records per site with movement and time, vehicle types
outputs: dominant pattern, share, matching remedies, suggested edits to test
existing: partial: analyse_safety (rear-end conflicts and severe ones per road); no movement classification or remedy table
notes: The remedy table is the knowledge base; ACMS can only simulate some remedies (turn pockets, roundabouts, speed).

idea: Self-enforcing speed reduction (Table 6.04, Fig 6.44): long humps (progressively more discomfort at higher speed, 40 mm rising to about 80 mm in a series), short sharp humps are driven fast and are dangerous/ineffective, bar markings and rumble strips act through perceived speed or noise, chicanes and lane narrowing, gateways at village entry (a narrowing plus a hump), road narrowing to cut crossing width, speed limits alone are abused without enforcement; humps near schools and where roads pass through settlements; advance warning required; area-wide 30 km/h zones with closures.
does: Road feature (hump, raised crossing, chicane, narrowing, gateway) placed at a distance along a road that sets a target crossing speed for vehicles (e.g. hump 20-30 km/h, chicane 30 km/h) with a deceleration approach and re-acceleration, and a pedestrian benefit flag; used in experiments to compare through speed, travel time, bus delay and conflicts, and by the context_target_speed tool.
inputs: road id, position, device type, target speed, length
outputs: road feature stored with the network; simulated speed profile, delay, conflicts
existing: none (not_built: road types do not change behaviour; vehicles follow only speed limit and curves)
notes: Needs a position-based speed cap in the car-following model (like a curve cap); keep clearly labelled as a placeholder with validated inputs.

topic: Automated road safety audit checklist with numeric rules
idea: Checklists B and C turned into tests: roads categorised into hierarchy; each street intersects only its own class or one above/below; arterials with 2+ lanes per direction have a median; access roads loops or cul-de-sacs no longer than 200 m; arterial-arterial junctions channelised signals, roundabouts or grade separated; arterial-collector priority T (priority to arterial), roundabout or signals; collector-access priority T; protected turn bay at arterial-collector junctions; arterial intersection spacing at least 250 m (at most 3 per km); no vehicle access within 50 m of an intersection; parking prohibited on arterials; pedestrian refuge 1.2 m minimum (2.0 m preferred) where 2+ lanes per direction, pedestrians never cross more than two lanes before a refuge; collector pedestrian crossings signalised if AADT above 7,500 veh/day; access street serving more than 100 dwellings or 200 jobs needs a footway; bicycle way 2 m, shared 2.5 m; stopping sight distance and curve radii above minimum for estimated speeds; every N 'no' answer cites the guidance section.
does: Runs the checklist as a deterministic audit over the open network, using inferred road classes (speed, lanes), junction control types, spacing between junctions, cul-de-sac lengths, institutions' doors (access within 50 m of a junction), crossings and daily volumes from the OD matrix, and returns pass/fail per question with the offending object ids, then the assistant explains and proposes edits; a second pass after edits shows what was fixed.
inputs: network, daily volumes per road from routing, institutions, crossings
outputs: checklist table: question, pass/fail, objects, cited rule and guidance, severity
existing: partial: analyse_network (validity, reachability, short roads, curve speed, roundabout size); no safety audit rules
notes: Thresholds (250 m, 50 m, 200 m, 7,500 veh/day, 2 m) are quoted from the guide for developing-country contexts; expose them as parameters. Complements check_design_standards and check_road_hierarchy.

topic: Turn bans and street closures with displacement
idea: Ban the turn that dominates conflicts relative to its volume (most often the turn across oncoming traffic, 'no right turn' for left-hand traffic) and provide the movement at a safer nearby location; closure types (intersection closure cuts 32 conflict points to 9, midblock closure, diagonal closure, half closure, footway widening) reduce through traffic but displace it; a median barrier at minor junctions bans crossing and turning through the main road and needs U-turn provision; bans need physical enforcement; displaced movements must be accommodated elsewhere.
does: Assistant tool to prohibit a turning movement (from road A to road B) or close a junction leg, which the router respects; reports the displaced flow (extra veh-km, new route volumes) and the conflicts removed (movement count from the conflict audit), and tests the change with paired seeds including the roads that receive diverted traffic.
inputs: junction, from-road, to-road, or closure type
outputs: restriction stored with the network; rerouted flows; conflict and delay change
existing: none (turn restrictions not built, not_built lists them only for OSM import)
notes: Needs the router (assign_routes, shortest path) and turn lane logic to accept forbidden transitions.

topic: Pedestrian crossing warrant PV squared and refuge rules
idea: UK crossing warrant: PV^2 with P the pedestrian flow per hour across a 100 m length centred on the site and V the two-way vehicle flow per hour; thresholds separate no formal crossing, zebra (priority rule, unsuitable for heavy fast traffic), pelican (signals: elderly, high speed, heavy pedestrian flow, bus lanes) and staggered pelican on dual carriageways or roads wider than 15 m; raised crossing 80-100 mm where drivers do not give way; refuges at least 1.8 m (never under 1.2 m), not opposite bus stops; pedestrian fences 500 mm from kerb, 1 m high.
does: Computes P (from institutions' walking trips and bus stop users near the road) and V (from the run or OD) for each road segment, evaluates PV^2 and recommends no crossing, refuge, zebra or signalised crossing, with a reason, and lists existing crossings that are not warranted or are missing; ties to pedestrian_crossing_check timing.
inputs: institutions (people, mode shares, walk catchment), traffic volume per road, road width, speed
outputs: per segment: P, V, PV^2, recommended crossing type, existing crossing verdict
existing: partial: describe (crossings), institution mode splits give walk trips; no warrant
notes: Threshold values are in Fig 6.55 (a graph not extracted); the usual UK values are about 1e8 for a zebra/pelican at low speed but confirm in the figure/Local Transport Note.

topic: Signal safety by phase position and clearance check
idea: Appendix B(e) diagnosis for signal accidents: split crashes by position in the green (beginning, middle, end) and by red overshoot; beginning-of-green turning crashes in wide junctions suggest a delayed start for oncoming traffic; middle-of-green turning crashes suggest fast oncoming speed or obscured view and a separate turn phase; end-of-green crashes suggest drivers beating the signal and an early cut-off; red running at approach speed above 50 km/h needs enough inter-green (all-red) to clear the junction before the opposing green; check that timings still suit current flows and that heads are visible; nose-to-tail collisions need protected turning bays; also separate RESTART (gap acceptance from stop) from OVERSHOOT (failure to stop) crashes at stop/give-way junctions since treatments differ.
does: For each signalised junction records, per simulated conflict, where in the signal cycle it happened (start/middle/end of green, amber, early red) and the approach speed, tabulates the distribution, flags dilemma-zone exposure (vehicles that neither stop nor clear at amber at over 50 km/h) and inter-green shortfall (clearance time needed from the stop line over junction length at the approach speed), and suggests all-red extension, delayed start, early cut-off or a protected turn phase, which optimise_signals can then test with a safety objective.
inputs: run conflicts with time and junction, signal phase log, approach speeds, junction size
outputs: conflict distribution by cycle position, dilemma-zone count, clearance time needed vs provided, suggested timing changes
existing: partial: analyse_safety (rear-end conflicts), optimise_signals (delay, throughput objectives), read_traffic (signal states); no safety objective or phase-position analysis
cite: App B s(e) Accidents at automatic traffic signals, items 1-9; E(b) restart vs overshoot
notes: Clearance time formula (all-red = (W + L)/v) comes from standard signal practice, not this text; AGENTS.md requires overrides to keep amber and all-red safe, so the tool only recommends.
